start: Settings, Restore from a backup, just after 'Replace' finished with 'Restored ...' shown

user_sees: Busy button 'Putting this phone back...'
must_not: A second tap starting a second undo

user_sees: 'Done. This phone is back to how it was before the restore.'
The 'Undo restore' button is gone
Old workouts, routines, settings and profile are back
must_not: The backup's photos left on the phone
The backup's settings kept after the undo

start: Same, after 'Add to what's here' finished

user_sees: 'Done. This phone is back to how it was before the restore.'
Only the workouts the backup added are gone
must_not: Workouts that were on the phone before the restore removed
Settings changed (Add never changed them)

start: Restore just finished from the welcome screen, or the member left the screen

steps.action: Look for 'Undo restore' after a welcome-screen restore
user_sees: No 'Undo restore' button
must_not: An undo button that wipes the only copy of the data

steps.action: Leave the restore screen and come back
user_sees: 'Choose backup file' again, no undo
must_not: An undo applied after the member logged new workouts, losing them

user_sees: 'Couldn't undo. Please try again.'
must_not: The phone left half-way between backup and old state with no word

steps.action: After 'Done. This phone is back...' look at the screen
user_sees: No undo button; the backup summary and note stay
must_not: A second 'Undo restore' that applies the old copy again

user_sees: A new restore and a new 'Undo restore'
must_not: The earlier undo copy reused

steps.action: Do step 2 of "Undo a restore" on the phone with the watch connected; look at both. Then do it from the watch.
user_sees: Phone and watch show the same saved data within a few seconds
must_not: Two different values on phone and watch, a double saved data made by both, or the watch stuck on the old state

note: The watch may have received the restored routines before the undo

start: Settings, Restore from a backup, just after 'Replace' finished with 'Restored ...' shown; set-up: many items (500+)

steps.action: Start "Undo a restore" when 500 or more saved data rows exist.
user_sees: The list opens in a few seconds and scrolls; every count is the true total
must_not: A count that stops at a page size, missing rows of saved data, or a screen that freezes

user_sees: Busy button 'Putting this phone back...'
must_not: A second tap starting a second undo

user_sees: 'Done. This phone is back to how it was before the restore.'

Old workouts, routines, settings and profile are back
must_not: The backup's photos left on the phone
The backup's settings kept after the undo
A count that stops at a page size, missing rows of saved data, or a screen that freezes

note: The safety copy of the whole database is held in memory; a phone with 500+ workouts and many photos may run short

start: Settings, Restore from a backup, just after 'Replace' finished with 'Restored ...' shown

user_sees: Busy button 'Putting this phone back...'
must_not: A second tap starting a second undo

steps.action: Press back at step 1 of "Undo a restore".
user_sees: The screen before, or a question to keep or drop what was typed
must_not: A half-saved saved data, typed text lost without a warning, or the app closing

note: The undo copy lives only in memory: closing the app during or after the restore loses the undo for good

start: Settings, Restore from a backup, just after 'Replace' finished with 'Restored ...' shown

user_sees: Busy button 'Putting this phone back...'
must_not: A second tap starting a second undo

steps.action: Close the app (swipe it away) at step 1 of "Undo a restore", then open it again.
user_sees: Either nothing was saved, or the saved data is whole; the app says which
must_not: A half-saved saved data, a double saved data after trying again, or a stuck screen on reopening

note: The undo copy lives only in memory: closing the app during or after the restore loses the undo for good

steps.action: Tap the main button of step 1 of "Undo a restore" twice, fast.

must_not: Two rows of saved data, two charges, two messages sent, or two screens opened

note: The undo copy lives only in memory: closing the app during or after the restore loses the undo for good
